declarations.name: KiAlert
declarations.description: A persistent inline status message with token-backed tone semantics.
declarations.whenToUse:
show a persistent inline message about the state of a page or
section, such as a failed save, completed operation, or service notice, that
remains until the condition is resolved or the person dismisses it. Express
severity with `tone`, never custom styling.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
transient confirmations that expire on their own belong to
`ki-toast`, raised into a `ki-toaster`; tiny status descriptors attached to
another element belong to `ki-badge`; blocking decisions belong to
`ki-dialog`; inline field-level validation belongs to the form control.

Assistive technology note: alerts that must be announced should be inserted
dynamically, or re-shown by clearing `dismissed`; alerts present at initial
page load are exposed with their role but platform announcement is not
guaranteed.

Every non-neutral alert should carry an icon: in the onmars theme the tone
is drawn on the icon alone.

attributes.name: dismiss-label
attributes.description:
Accessible name for the dismiss button. Override for localization; the
default English string is the component's only built-in user-visible text.

When to use: provide a localized action name whenever the document language
is not English.
When NOT to use: do not put the alert message here; use the default slot.

attributes.name: dismissed
attributes.description:
Reflected dismissed state. User dismissal sets it; applications may also
set or clear it. While true, the host remains in the document but renders no
alert subtree and leaves the accessibility tree. Clearing it re-shows the
alert and creates a dynamic live-region appearance.

When to use: persist or restore acknowledgement state from application
data.
When NOT to use: do not listen for programmatic changes as dismissal
events; `ki-dismiss` is only for user activation.

attributes.name: dismissible
attributes.description:
Renders one native dismiss button when true. The button sits outside the
live-region boundary, so its accessible name is not announced as part of
the alert message. When false, the alert adds no tab stop.

When to use: allow a person to acknowledge and clear a persistent message.
When NOT to use: do not use dismissible for auto-expiring messages; those
belong to `ki-toast`.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description:
Optional emphasized text rendered before the message inside the live
region. Empty strings render no heading. The heading is a `strong`
element, not a document heading, so it never changes page outline.

When to use: add a short label when it helps identify the status message.
When NOT to use: do not use heading for page structure; use a real heading
outside the alert when the document needs one.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description:
Semantic intent for visual styling and live-region urgency. `danger` and
`warning` expose `role="alert"`; `neutral`, `success`, `info`, absent, and
unrecognized values expose `role="status"`. Unknown values keep rendering
and fall back to the neutral token matrix by CSS construction.

When to use: choose the tone that describes the page or section state.
When NOT to use: do not use tone for layout, density, or filled-vs-outlined
styling; those are token/theme decisions.

events.name: ki-dismiss
events.description:
Fired once after the user dismisses the alert — emitted after the alert is
hidden and focus has been handed to the next control. `detail` is `null`
and the event is not cancelable (the alert is already gone when it runs).
When to use: record acknowledgement, or advance an application flow after a
user closes the alert.
When NOT to use: do not treat it as a veto point, and do not expect it for
programmatic `dismissed` changes — it fires only for user activation.

slots.description: Message body. It lives inside the live-region boundary.

slots.name: actions
slots.description:
Optional responses to this message, in a row at the bottom
of the card, outside the live region. Slot `size="sm"` buttons. The alert
never activates them and an action does not dismiss the alert; the
application does, by setting `dismissed`. When NOT to use: a response the
person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.

slots.name: icon
slots.description:
Optional decorative glyph shown in a round frame at the top of
the card, in the tone's colors. Hidden from assistive technology: it never
carries meaning the heading and message lack. When to use: give every
non-neutral alert an icon. When NOT to use: never as the only cue for the
message.

declarations.name: KiAvatar
declarations.description:
A static identity visual that shows a person or entity at a glance through
a fallback chain: portrait, then initials, then a built-in generic figure.
declarations.whenToUse:
a compact identity visual for a person or entity — a comment
author, a contact list item, a project member. Set `label` whenever the
avatar is the only carrier of the identity (no adjacent visible name);
compose several into `ki-avatar-group` for a compact "who is involved"
stack with overflow.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
as a clickable control (compose the avatar inside an
interactive host such as ki-button), for logos or arbitrary illustrations
(plain `img`), or unlabeled when no adjacent text names the identity.
Use the counter slot for a decorative count or presence dot.

attributes.name: initials
attributes.description:
Initials rendered verbatim as the second fallback step — never derived
from the label, never truncated (FR-003). Catalog guidance: one to two
characters. With a label present the initials are presentational;
assistive technology receives the label alone.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name for the identity ("Ana García"). With a label the avatar
is exposed as a named non-interactive image (role `img`) in every content
mode — the portrait never carries a second alternative text of its own.
Without a label the avatar is decorative and contributes nothing to the
accessibility tree; the identity must then live in adjacent visible text
(FR-002).

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Size step over the shared scale; per-size metrics (box, initials font,
figure glyph) are per-theme component tokens, never hardcoded (FR-004).
An unrecognized value matches no style selector, so the avatar keeps the
default medium metrics (fallback by CSS construction, FR-007).

attributes.name: src
attributes.description:
Portrait URL, the first step of the fallback chain. When it fails to
load — initially or at runtime — the avatar silently falls back to the
initials (or the generic figure) with no error, no layout change and no
event (FR-001). Loading policy follows the platform image defaults.

cssProperties.description: color used by the avatar component for the initials/figure surface: Surface/primary_med_em, the exact variable behind the Type=text gradient start and the Type=icon solid fill. declarations.name: KiAvatarGroup
declarations.description:
A token-styled companion container that stacks `ki-avatar` children as one
overlapping row with a configurable visible cap and a static "+N" overflow
counter.
declarations.whenToUse:
a compact "who is involved" stack — the members of a shared
document, project card or event row — where space deserves only the first
few identities and an exact "+N" counter accounts for the rest.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
as a member picker or expandable overflow (future interactive
grouping — the counter is static text, never a button), for a single
identity (use `ki-avatar` alone), or with children other than `ki-avatar`
(foreign markup is unsupported and not repaired, 016 precedent).

attributes.name: max
attributes.description:
Visible cap for the member stack. When the member count exceeds it, the
first `max` members render followed by a "+N" counter accounting exactly
for the hidden rest. Without it — or when it is not a positive whole
number — every member renders and no counter appears; malformed
agent-generated markup never breaks the page (FR-009, S14, S15).

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Size step governing the metrics of every visible member and the counter
(avatar vocabulary, FR-010). Member-declared sizes are overridden inside
a group so the stack stays uniform (S6). An unrecognized value matches
no style selector, so the group keeps the default medium metrics
(FR-007).

members.name: max
members.description:
Visible cap for the member stack. When the member count exceeds it, the
first `max` members render followed by a "+N" counter accounting exactly
for the hidden rest. Without it — or when it is not a positive whole
number — every member renders and no counter appears; malformed
agent-generated markup never breaks the page (FR-009, S14, S15).

(FR-007).

slots.description:
`ki-avatar` members, stacked in source order. Members beyond the
visible cap are neither rendered nor exposed to assistive technology.

declarations.name: KiBadge
declarations.description: A static, non-interactive status pill.
declarations.whenToUse:
annotate an entity with short status text (a state, a
category) whose meaning is carried by the label itself; the tone color
only reinforces the text, it never replaces it.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
feedback that must be announced (that is
ki-alert's job — the badge has no live region), an interactive
chip, filter or button, empty content (the label IS the meaning), or a
notification-counter overlay (use ki-counter).

attributes.name: size

onmars, with 12px text at every size. An unrecognized value falls back to
the `md` metrics the same way.

the `--ki-badge-{tone}-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no
style selector, so the badge keeps the neutral appearance (fallback by
CSS construction — no validation code).

declarations.name: KiButton
declarations.description: A token-styled action button with native button semantics.
declarations.whenToUse:
trigger the single main action of a view, supporting actions
in descending hierarchy, or confirming/destructive actions through tone.
While the action a button started is in progress, set `loading` on that
button instead of disabling it.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
navigation, icon-only actions, persistent toggles, or the
progress of a page or region (use ki-progress).

attributes.name: command
attributes.description:
Dialog action to run for `commandfor`. Use `show-modal` to open,
`close` for direct dismissal, or `request-close` for guarded dismissal.
Choose a command for local dialog control and omit it for other actions.

attributes.name: commandfor
attributes.description:
ID of a ki-dialog in the same document or shadow tree as this button.
Set it together with `command` to connect a dialog declaratively.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Prevents activation, removes the button from keyboard reach, and exposes
the unavailable state through the internal native button. Wins over
`loading` when both are set.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics; use
`loading`.

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description:
Pending state of the action this button started (saving, sending).
While set, every activation is blocked (pointer, Enter and Space) and the
button neither submits nor resets its form, but it stays focusable, in
the Tab order and at its width: the label stays laid out, transparent,
and a spinner is drawn in its place. The internal native button is
exposed with `aria-disabled="true"` and keeps its name, and
`loadingLabel` is announced as a polite status message. `disabled`, and
a disabled fieldset, win over it. The application sets it when the
action starts and clears it when the action ends.
When to use: while the work a click on this button started is running,
so a second activation cannot repeat it.
When NOT to use: for a button the person cannot use yet (use
`disabled`), or for the progress of a page or region (use ki-progress).

attributes.name: loading-label
attributes.description:
Text of the polite status message announced while `loading` is set.
Override for localization; the default English string is the button's
only built-in user-visible text.
When to use: provide a localized message whenever the document language
is not English, or a more specific one ("Saving").
When NOT to use: do not repeat the button's label here; the person
already hears it on focus.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key contributed when this button submits its form.
When NOT to use: omit when no submitter value should be sent.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed button size. Every size keeps at least the minimum pointer
target; choose the size that matches the density of the surrounding UI.
When NOT to use: do not use `ki-button` for icon-only compact controls.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description:
Semantic intent for the action, independent of hierarchy. Use `success`
for confirming actions and `danger` for destructive actions.
When NOT to use: do not use tone for visual hierarchy; use `variant`.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
Native form action type: `submit` submits the owning form (running
constraint validation and contributing `name`/`value` to the form data),
`reset` restores field defaults, `button` never touches the form.
A configured dialog command takes precedence over the form action.
Cancel a submission from the form's `submit` event (`preventDefault()`);
unlike a native button, `preventDefault()` on the `click` event does not
cancel it. During submission `event.submitter` is a transient native
button carrying this element's `name`/`value`, not the `ki-button` host.
When NOT to use: use `button` when the action must never submit a form.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Form-data value paired with `name` when this button submits its form.
When NOT to use: omit when the default empty submitter value is intended.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
Visual hierarchy for the action. Use filled `primary` for the single main
action, outlined `secondary` for supporting actions, `quaternary` for
neutral text actions, and `ghost` for accent text actions.
When NOT to use: do not use variant to signal success or danger; use
`tone` for intent.

Cancel a submission from the form's `submit` event (`preventDefault()`);
unlike a native button, `preventDefault()` on the `click` event does not
cancel it. During submission `event.submitter` is a transient native
button carrying this element's `name`/`value`, not the `ki-button` host.
When NOT to use: use `button` when the action must never submit a form.

members.name: value
members.description:
Form-data value paired with `name` when this button submits its form.
When NOT to use: omit when the default empty submitter value is intended.

members.name: variant
members.description:
Visual hierarchy for the action. Use filled `primary` for the single main
action, outlined `secondary` for supporting actions, `quaternary` for
neutral text actions, and `ghost` for accent text actions.
When NOT to use: do not use variant to signal success or danger; use
`tone` for intent.

declarations.name: KiCheckbox
declarations.description:
A form-associated checkbox for selecting independent options.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).
declarations.whenToUse:
selecting one or more independent options that a form submits
later, including a "select all" parent that presents partial selection with
`indeterminate`. Always provide a visible label in the default slot.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
a single mutually exclusive choice, an immediate on/off
effect, triggering an action, unlabeled/icon-only usage, or
`checked="false"` to mean unchecked. Boolean attributes use presence
semantics; omit `checked` to express unchecked.

attributes.name: checked
attributes.description:
Live binary selection state. User activation by pointer, slotted label or
Space toggles it with native checkbox parity and emits composed `input`
before composed `change`. Boolean presence semantics apply:
`checked="false"` still renders checked; omit the attribute to express
unchecked. Programmatic assignment is silent.
When NOT to use: do not treat this reflected attribute as a native
`defaultChecked`; reset uses the baseline captured at form association.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Prevents activation, removes the checkbox from keyboard reach, exposes the
unavailable state, and excludes it from form data.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for validation errors or pending
state.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description:
Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` checkbox is
left unchecked, and its `validationMessage`. Say what checking it means
("Accept the terms to continue"). Without it the browser's own message
shows, in the browser's language. An error set with `setCustomValidity`
outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; call
`setCustomValidity` for those.

attributes.name: help-text
attributes.description:
One line of help under the checkbox, read with it as its description:
what checking it means or commits to.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

attributes.name: indeterminate
attributes.description:
Presentation-only mixed state. It renders the dash mark, is forwarded to
the internal native input for mixed assistive-technology exposure, and
never changes the submitted value. Any user toggle clears it and removes
the reflected attribute.
When NOT to use: do not submit or persist `indeterminate` as a third
value; model data remains binary through `checked`.

attributes.name: label-hint
attributes.description:
Short text shown after the slotted label and read with it as part of the
checkbox name, so people know before submitting whether they must check
it: "(required)" on a consent the form cannot do without, "(optional)"
on one it can, in the page's own language. It changes no validation; set
`required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put what checking it commits to in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key contributed when the checkbox is checked.
When NOT to use: omit when the checkbox should not submit a value.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description:
Requires the checkbox to be checked before form submission can proceed.
The invalid appearance appears after a blocked submission attempt or an
invalidating user toggle, never on initial render.
When NOT to use: do not use required to express group-level rules; compose
those at the form/application layer.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed size: the box is 18, 20 or 24px in onmars. `sm` also takes
the smaller label (13/20, 8px away); `md` and `lg` keep the 15px label.
The pointer target never drops under 24px. An unrecognized value matches
no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the text and controls around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Form-data value paired with `name` when checked. If omitted, the submitted
value is `on`, matching native checkbox behavior.
When NOT to use: do not encode the unchecked state here; unchecked
checkboxes contribute no form entry.

declarations.name: KiDialog
declarations.description: A modal dialog for one interrupting decision or short focused task.
declarations.whenToUse:
destructive confirmations, blocking choices, and brief
critical input that must be resolved before returning to the page. Always
provide a `heading`, place actions in the `footer` slot, wire each
dismissal to `close()` or a close command, and in destructive confirmations put `autofocus` on
the least destructive action.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
non-blocking feedback (`ki-alert`, `ki-toast`),
supplementary hints (`ki-tooltip`), long forms or multi-step flows
(navigate or use a future full-screen variant), menus, or pickers.

attributes.name: close-on-backdrop
attributes.description:
Opts into backdrop light-dismiss. Omit this attribute for critical
confirmations; `close-on-backdrop="false"` still enables it.
When to use: low-risk dialogs where an outside click may safely dismiss.
When NOT to use: destructive confirmations or decisions that should not be
lost to a stray click; omit the attribute entirely rather than setting it
to `"false"`.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description:
Visible dialog title and accessible-name source. Always provide a heading;
an empty value intentionally leaves the native dialog unnamed.
When to use: name the interrupting decision, for example "Delete
account?". When NOT to use: do not omit it for production dialogs; APG
modal dialogs require an accessible name.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description:
Reflected live modal state. Add it or call `show()` to open; remove it or
call `close()` to close. When open, the native dialog enters the top layer
and the page behind is inert.
When to use: bind application state to the dialog's modal lifecycle.
When NOT to use: do not set the internal native `<dialog open>` attribute;
the host attribute is the only public source of truth.

members.name: closeOnBackdrop
members.description:
Opts into backdrop light-dismiss. Omit this attribute for critical
confirmations; `close-on-backdrop="false"` still enables it.
When to use: low-risk dialogs where an outside click may safely dismiss.
When NOT to use: destructive confirmations or decisions that should not be
lost to a stray click; omit the attribute entirely rather than setting it
to `"false"`.

members.name: heading
members.description:
Visible dialog title and accessible-name source. Always provide a heading;
an empty value intentionally leaves the native dialog unnamed.
When to use: name the interrupting decision, for example "Delete
account?". When NOT to use: do not omit it for production dialogs; APG
modal dialogs require an accessible name.

members.name: open
members.description:
Reflected live modal state. Add it or call `show()` to open; remove it or
call `close()` to close. When open, the native dialog enters the top layer
and the page behind is inert.
When to use: bind application state to the dialog's modal lifecycle.
When NOT to use: do not set the internal native `<dialog open>` attribute;
the host attribute is the only public source of truth.

members.name: close
members.description:
Closes the dialog and reports `method`. No-op when already closed.
Equivalent to removing the host `open` attribute. Footer actions never
close automatically; wire them to this method or an invoker command.
When to use: resolve footer actions, programmatic dismissals, and
application-controlled cancellation. When NOT to use: do not use for
Escape or backdrop bookkeeping; those paths set their own close reasons.

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the dialog modally. No-op when already open. Equivalent to adding
the host `open` attribute.
When to use: call from the invoker that should receive focus again after
close. When NOT to use: do not call repeatedly to refresh content; update
slotted content directly while open.

events.name: ki-close
events.description:
Post-close notification for every close path. Footer actions report
`method` when they call `close()`, Escape reports `escape`, and opt-in
backdrop dismissal reports `backdrop`. Invoker dismissals report `command`.
When to use: update application state after the dialog is already closed
and focus has returned through the native mechanism.
When NOT to use: do not expect this event to veto closing; it is not
cancelable in v1.

declarations.name: KiDivider
declarations.description: A static, decorative rule that visually separates adjacent content.
declarations.whenToUse:
visually separate adjacent content when spacing alone is not
enough: grouped settings sections, toolbar action groups, distinct
regions inside a card — horizontal between stacked content, vertical
between side-by-side content.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
between list items (separation is a ki-list theme-token
decision), semantic thematic breaks in running prose (native `<hr>`
carries those semantics — the divider is deliberately decorative and
contributes no role, name or announcement), as a border or outline
substitute (surface/border tokens), or purely decorative flourishes
(prefer white space).

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description:
Layout axis of the rule: `horizontal` spans the available inline size
between stacked content; `vertical` stretches to the cross size its
layout context provides, between side-by-side content. A structural
axis, never appearance — thickness, color, end caps and gutter are
per-theme `--ki-divider-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no
style selector, so the divider keeps the default horizontal rendering
(fallback by CSS construction — no validation code).

declarations.name: KiIconButton
declarations.description:
A token-styled, icon-only action button with native button semantics and a
mandatory accessible name.
declarations.whenToUse:
a compact, widely understood action where space precludes a
visible label: toolbars, card and dialog corners (close), media transport,
data-row actions. Always supply `label`; usually pair with ki-tooltip for
sighted discoverability. While the action it started is in progress, set
`loading` instead of disabling it.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
whenever a visible label fits (use ki-button), toggling
state without supplying `pressed`, navigation (use a link), or form
submit/reset (ki-icon-button is not form-associated; use ki-button, whose
visible label communicates the consequence).

attributes.name: command
attributes.description:
Dialog action to run for `commandfor`. Use `show-modal` to open,
`close` for direct dismissal, or `request-close` for guarded dismissal.
Choose a command for local dialog control and omit it for other actions.

attributes.name: commandfor
attributes.description:
ID of a ki-dialog in the same document or shadow tree as this button.
Set it together with `command` to connect a dialog declaratively.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Prevents activation, removes the icon button from keyboard reach, and
exposes the unavailable state through the internal native button. Wins
over `loading` when both are set.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics; use
`loading`.

attributes.name: expanded
attributes.description:
Application-owned disclosure state for a trigger that opens a popup.
The native icon button exposes this as `aria-expanded`. Use with
`aria-haspopup="menu"` for a menu trigger. Omit for other actions.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name of the internal focusable button ("Close", "Play").
Required in the catalog contract: the icon is presentational, so without
a label the control exposes no name and fails the accessibility audit.
The component never invents a fallback name.
When NOT to use: never omit it; never duplicate it as visible text (a
visible label means ki-button).

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description:
Pending state of the action this icon button started (refreshing,
sending). While set, every activation is blocked (pointer, Enter and
Space), but the icon button stays focusable, in the Tab order and at its
size: the icon stays laid out, transparent, and a spinner is drawn in its
place. The internal native button is exposed with `aria-disabled="true"`
and keeps its `label`, and `loadingLabel` is announced as a polite status
message. `disabled` wins over it. The application sets it when the
action starts and clears it when the action ends.
When to use: while the work a click on this icon button started is
running, so a second activation cannot repeat it.
When NOT to use: for an icon button the person cannot use yet (use
`disabled`), or for the progress of a page or region (use ki-progress).

attributes.name: loading-label
attributes.description:
Text of the polite status message announced while `loading` is set.
Override for localization; the default English string is the icon
button's only built-in user-visible text.
When to use: provide a localized message whenever the document language
is not English, or a more specific one ("Refreshing").
When NOT to use: do not repeat `label` here; the person already hears it
on focus.

attributes.name: pressed
attributes.description:
Application-owned toggle state. The native icon button exposes this as
`aria-pressed`. Omit for a momentary action.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed square size. Every size keeps at least the 24×24 minimum
pointer target (`xs` sits exactly on it); choose the size that matches
the density of the surrounding UI.
When NOT to use: do not shrink below `xs` through tokens; no theme may
go under the WCAG 2.2 pointer-target floor.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description:
Semantic intent for the action, independent of hierarchy. Use `success`
for confirming actions and `danger` for destructive actions.
When NOT to use: do not use tone for visual hierarchy; use `variant`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
Visual hierarchy for the action. Use filled `primary` for the single main
action, outlined `secondary` for supporting actions, `quaternary` for
neutral icon actions, and `ghost` for accent icon actions.
When NOT to use: do not use variant to signal success or danger; use
`tone` for intent.

declarations.name: KiImage
declarations.description:
Displays one accessible image in a reserved frame, with an optional caption
and a fallback if the source is refused or fails to load.
declarations.whenToUse:
to show a photo, illustration, or diagram with a predictable
layout. Supply task-relevant alt text, or mark purely decorative media as
decorative. Set an explicit ratio when the layout must stay fixed.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
for a background decoration, a video, or an interactive
control. Use a separate control to open or otherwise act on an image.

attributes.name: alt
attributes.description:
Describe what the image shows for the task at hand. Required and nonblank
for an informative image. Omit it for a decorative image.

attributes.name: decorative
attributes.description: Hide the media from assistive technology when it conveys no information.

attributes.name: fallback-label
attributes.description:
Localizable fallback label. An informative fallback appends the image's
description, when available, to this label.

attributes.name: fit
attributes.description: Cover fills the frame. Contain preserves the whole image in it.

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description: Native loading hint. Use eager for a critical image above the fold.

attributes.name: radius
attributes.description: Corner radius of the media frame.

attributes.name: ratio
attributes.description:
An explicit ratio reserves the same frame before load and on failure.
Auto reserves 16:9 first and uses the intrinsic ratio after load.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: Relative or HTTP(S) image URL. Refused sources are left unloaded.

events.name: ki-error

Reports a load failure or rejected URL once per source attempt. Bubbles
and crosses shadow boundaries so consumers can observe it on a surface.

declarations.name: KiIndicator
declarations.description:
A non-interactive page-position indicator: one dot per position of a
bounded sequence, exactly one highlighted as current.
declarations.whenToUse:
show the current position within a bounded, sequential set of
peer views whose navigation lives elsewhere: carousel slides, unlabeled
onboarding steps, gallery pages. Wire `count` and `current` (1-based) to
the sequence the consumer renders and give it a `label` (required
authoring: assistive technology reads one graphic named
"<label>, <current> / <count>"). Below two positions an indicator carries
no information.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
section navigation (ki-tabs), task completion or loading
(ki-progress), labeled step flows (a stepper is a separate roadmap item),
interactive pagination (a future feature — the indicator takes no focus
and no input; navigation belongs to the composing carousel's own
controls), or conveying quantity without a current position. Position
changes are never announced by the indicator itself (no live region): the
composing carousel owns announcements.

attributes.name: count
attributes.description:
Number of positions (non-negative integer): one dot renders per
position, in position order. A missing, non-numeric or negative value
renders zero dots — an authoring mistake by catalog guidance, never an
error state or a rendering failure (FR-002; empty ki-list precedent).
At most 20 positions render, and the catalog accepts no more: the
indicator serves a short sequence of peer views, 20 dots are the longest
row that fits a 320 CSS px viewport (the WCAG reflow width) in both
shipped themes, and one dot renders per position, so the bound also caps
the work a single node can demand. A larger value renders 20.

attributes.name: current
attributes.description:
The current position, 1-based to match the exposed position text
("2 / 5"). Exactly one dot presents the current appearance whenever
`count` >= 1: values above `count` clamp to the last position, values
below 1 and non-numeric values fall back to the first (FR-003). Updates
re-render in place — the highlight and the exposed text follow
immediately, re-applying the normalization (FR-004). The catalog accepts
1 to 20, the positions a bounded `count` can have.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name of the sequence ("Slide position"). The exposed name
combines it with the wordless numeric position —
"<label>, <current> / <count>" — on a single non-interactive graphic;
without a label the name degrades to the bare position text (documented
as required authoring, FR-005). The label is never rendered visually
and position changes are never announced (no live region, FR-006).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-block-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot block size: the 8px circle diameter measured in the State=inactive vector (the 16px frame height is row alignment, carried by the current dot).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the indicator component for the resting dot fill: Inverse_white/alpha_48 (Black/48 light, White/48 dark) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Inverse_white/alpha_18, which reads 1.53:1 light and 1.64:1 dark against the page; alpha_48 is the first step of the same ramp that clears the 3:1 FR-012 and WCAG 1.4.11 ask. The scheme flip rides the semantic layer.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-block-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot block size: Space/3xl, the exact variable bound as the 16px height of the State=active pill (the full row line; declared family extension, design-extraction §Decisiones).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the indicator component for the current dot treatment: Inverse_white/alpha_48, the same step as the resting dots — the MarsUI State=active ring vector binds the variable of the resting fill, and its alpha_18 reads 1.53-1.64:1 against the page (declared a11y deviation, FR-012). Painted as the pill ring in onmars, where elongation carries the state; as the solid dot in themes that zero the hole.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-hole-block-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the block size of the transparent hole cut from the current pill: the 6px cutout height measured in the State=active vector; the ring width derives by construction as (current block size − hole block size) / 2 and a theme resolves it to zero for a solid dot (declared family extension, design-extraction §Decisiones).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-inline-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot inline size: Space/10xl, the exact variable bound as the 32px width of the State=active pill — the MarsUI elongation lives here, never in an attribute (FR-007).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-radius
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the pill is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-inline-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot inline size: Space/md, the exact variable bound as the 8px width of the State=inactive symbol; the painted circle is 8x8 centered in the 16px row line.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-radius
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the round dot is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-gap
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the space between dots: Space/sm, the exact variable bound as the 6px gap of the composed Nav_indicator row (node 14195:5866, specs/024-ki-indicator/design-extraction.md).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-motion-duration
cssProperties.description: duration used by the indicator component for the highlight transfer between dots: the Figma set documents no motion, so onmars resolves the single transition to the fast semantic duration (FR-008; disabled under reduced motion by construction).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-motion-easing
cssProperties.description: easing used by the indicator component for the highlight-transfer transition (MarsUI standard curve; previously the UA default ease applied).

cssProperties.name: --ki-motion-duration-fast
cssProperties.description: Fast interaction transition duration.

cssProperties.description: Utility entrance curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-decelerate. onmars: the MarsUI decelerate curve (ki.easing.out).

declarations.name: KiInput
declarations.description:
A token-styled single-line text field with native input semantics.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).
declarations.whenToUse:
collect one line of free text from a person, always with a
visible `label`; choose the `type` and `autocomplete` that match the entry
purpose.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
multiline text, predefined choices, boolean state, numeric
stepper entry, or placeholder-only labeling.

attributes.name: autocomplete
attributes.description:
Native autocomplete detail token forwarded to the internal input.
When NOT to use: omit when no autofill entry purpose is known.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Prevents editing, removes the field from keyboard reach and exposes the
unavailable state through the internal native input.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for readonly reference values.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description:
Message shown in place of the help text once the person's answer fails a
constraint (`required`, `type`), and the field's `validationMessage`. Say
how to fix the answer ("Enter an email address like name@example.com").
Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An
error set with `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; call
`setCustomValidity` for those.

attributes.name: help-text
attributes.description:
One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: the
format expected, or why the answer is asked. While an error shows, the
error takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Visible label rendered next to the entry area and used as the accessible
name. This is mandatory for valid usage.
When NOT to use: never use `placeholder` as a label substitute.

attributes.name: label-hint
attributes.description:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the field's
name, so people know before submitting whether to answer: "(optional)" on
the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or "(required)" the
other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation;
set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions or formats in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key for the submitted value.
When NOT to use: omit when the field must not contribute named form data.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description:
Hint shown when the field is empty.
When NOT to use: do not use placeholder as the accessible name.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description:
Makes the value focusable and selectable while rejecting edits.
When NOT to use: use `disabled` when the value must be unavailable and
excluded from forms.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description:
Marks the field as required for native constraint validation.
When NOT to use: do not use required on optional fields.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed field size (`--ki-input-{size}-*` tokens): the field box is
24, 32, 40, 48 or 56px tall in onmars, with its padding, radius, text and
icon box; the label and help text follow in three steps. An unrecognized
value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the buttons and fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
Entry kind with native single-line input semantics. Unknown runtime
values fall back to `text`; `number` is not a v1 input kind.
When NOT to use: use future numeric controls for locale-aware number entry.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Live text value. The attribute declares the initial default; the property
is the current value and programmatic assignments are silent.
Deviation from native (deliberate, research D2): assigning the ATTRIBUTE
programmatically also replaces the displayed value, silently — native
inputs would keep the user's dirty value. Form reset restores the
attribute's current value.
When NOT to use: do not observe user edits by polling; listen for `input`
and `change` (both re-dispatched composed across the shadow boundary).

declarations.name: KiLink

declarations.whenToUse: navigate to a page, section, or resource. Use a descriptive label and keep the default underline in running text. Leave the action binding unset for native navigation.
declarations.whenNotToUse: perform an action on the current page. Use ki-button variant="ghost" for that.

announcement. An explicit download still follows native download rules.

where placement identifies the link and keyboard focus still underlines it.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed row size (`--ki-list-item-{size}-*` tokens): minimum height
(48, 56, 64 or 72px with a secondary line in onmars), padding, gap and
text. Slotted start and end content keeps the size its author gave it.
An unrecognized value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: give every row of one list the same size.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

declarations.name: KiProgress
declarations.description:
A token-styled, non-interactive progress indicator for known or unknown
duration work.
declarations.whenToUse:
communicate advancement of an ongoing task such as upload,
download, installation or multi-step processing. Use `value`/`max` when
the completed fraction is known; use `indeterminate` when work is ongoing
but its duration cannot be measured, including loading-indicator use cases.
Choose `linear` in page flows and lists, and `circular` in compact or
centered placements. Always set `label` to what is progressing.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
static measurements within a known range such as disk
usage or scores (gauge/meter), step-by-step wizard navigation (stepper),
skeleton placeholders while content loads, or operations that finish in
under about one second.

attributes.name: indeterminate
attributes.description:
Unknown-duration mode. When set, no completed fraction or current value is
exposed. Its motion is declared only when reduced motion is not requested.
When to use: show ongoing work whose duration or total cannot be measured.
When NOT to use: do not use for known fractions; use `value` and `max`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name applied to the internal progressbar. Always set this to
what is progressing, such as "Uploading report.pdf". Without it the
element renders but exposes no accessible name, so the catalog contract
requires it.
When NOT to use: do not use a generic label such as "Loading" when the
task can be named more specifically.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description:
Total amount. Non-finite, zero or negative values normalize to `100` for
presentation and ARIA.
When to use: set when a determinate task's total is not 100.
When NOT to use: omit for conventional percentage-style progress.

attributes.name: shape
attributes.description:
Structural presentation. Use `linear` in page flows and lists; use
`circular` in compact or centered placements. Unknown values render linear.
When NOT to use: do not use shape to encode semantic status or task intent.

declarations.name: KiQr
declarations.description:
A machine-scannable QR code that hands a declared value — a link, a
pairing payload — from the screen to a nearby camera, encoded locally
and restyled entirely through tokens.
declarations.whenToUse:
hand a URL or machine-readable payload from the screen to a
nearby camera device: login pairing, tickets and passes, "continue on
mobile" links, Wi-Fi sharing. Declare `value` (encoded verbatim, always
locally) and a purpose-stating `label` ("Open onmars.dev on your phone"),
and always offer the same payload through an accessible alternative next
to the code — a visible link or copyable text — because a QR code is only
useful to someone who can point a second device's camera at the screen.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
data the person must read on this same screen (render text
or a link), one-dimensional barcodes (out of scope), anything interactive
(a QR code is not a button — pair it with a real control instead), secret
values (anyone who can photograph the screen can decode them), or as the
sole carrier of the payload (the accessible alternative is mandatory
guidance). An always-empty ki-qr and a value beyond the ~2,331-byte
capacity are authoring mistakes: both render nothing, silently.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name stating the code's purpose ("Open onmars.dev on your
phone"). The component exposes exactly one non-interactive image named
by it, falling back to the encoded value when absent (FR-005) — never
an unnamed graphic. The label is never rendered visually, and naming
the purpose is what tells assistive-technology users to look for the
accessible alternative carrying the same payload (documented catalog
guidance, FR-013).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
The exact text the code encodes — the single source of the content,
encoded locally as one UTF-8 byte segment at error-correction level M
(non-ASCII text additionally carries the UTF-8 ECI designator, so real
scanners decode the declared string rather than an ISO-8859-1
misreading), so an independent decoder recovers it byte-for-byte,
including non-ASCII text (FR-001), and no network request is ever made — the value is
data, never behavior: the component never interprets, resolves,
navigates to or fetches it (FR-002). Changes re-encode in place. When
absent, empty or beyond the capacity of the densest symbol (~2,331
bytes at level M), nothing renders and nothing errors (FR-003).

declarations.name: KiRadioGroup
declarations.description:
A token-styled radio group that owns selection, keyboard coordination and
form participation for slotted `ki-radio` options.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).
declarations.whenToUse:
a person must choose exactly one of a small set of mutually
exclusive options that should all be visible at once.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
many options or tight space (use `ki-select`), independent
on/off settings (use `ki-checkbox` or `ki-switch`), multiple selection, or
authored selection on options; set this group's `value` instead.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Makes the whole group unavailable, skips it in Tab order and removes its
form entry.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description:
Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` group is left
without a choice, and its `validationMessage` ("Choose a plan"). Without
it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An error
set with `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; call
`setCustomValidity` for those.

attributes.name: help-text
attributes.description:
One line of help under the options, read with the group as its
description: what the choice decides. While an error shows, the error
takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Visible label and accessible-name source for the radiogroup.
When NOT to use: do not omit it; unlabeled groups fail accessibility gates.

attributes.name: label-hint
attributes.description:
Short text shown after the group label and read with it as part of the
radiogroup name, so people know before submitting whether to choose:
"(optional)" on the few optional questions of a mostly required form, or
"(required)" the other way round, in the page's own language. It changes
no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put what the choice decides in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key for the selected option's value. Omit when the group should
not contribute a form entry.
When NOT to use: do not put `name` on `ki-radio` options; their internal
native inputs are intentionally unnamed.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description:
Requires one selected option for form submission. The group uses platform
`valueMissing` from its internal native radio inputs.
When NOT to use: do not use required when no answer is acceptable.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed size of every `ki-radio` the group holds: the circle is 18
or 20px in onmars, and `sm` takes the smaller option label (13/20, 8px
away). The group decides for all its options; the group's own label,
help and error keep their size. An unrecognized value matches no style
rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the text and controls around the group.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Projection of the current selection. The initial attribute selects the
first matching option; unmatched values leave the group unselected and
operable. Assigning the property updates selection silently.
When NOT to use: never author selection on `ki-radio`; set this value.

declarations.name: KiScroller
declarations.description:
A bounded scroll container that clips its content along one declared axis
and replaces platform scrollbar chrome with a token-resolved indicator.
declarations.whenToUse:
a bounded region inside a view whose content can outgrow it:
chat or message panes, code and log blocks, tag rows, sidebar navigation,
tall menus inside cards. Give it bounds (its size comes entirely from your
layout) and a `label` (required: the accessible name of the scroll
region). Scrolling stays native — wheel, touch, keyboard and indicator
drag operate the viewport directly.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
page-level scrolling (the browser's job), carousels or
paginated media (future indicator/carousel patterns), virtualized long
collections, multi-column tabular data, or nesting scrollers (v1
guarantees a single scroll axis per region). Cross-axis overflow is an
authoring mistake: the scroller scrolls its declared axis only and clips
the other — wrap or size content on the cross axis.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name of the scroll region ("Release notes", "Chat
messages"). Assistive technology receives a `region` with this name
whose slotted content keeps its own semantics (FR-006). Documented as
required: a scroller without a label renders but exposes no accessible
name and fails the accessibility audit (015-ki-progress precedent).
The label is never rendered visually.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description:
Declared scroll axis, mapping the design source's `Type` axis:
`vertical` (default) scrolls the block axis, `horizontal` the inline
axis. One axis per instance; the cross axis clips. A structural axis,
never appearance — thickness, shape and colors of the indicator are
per-theme `--ki-scroller-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no
style selector and no `horizontal` code path, so the scroller keeps
the default vertical behavior (fallback by CSS construction plus a
single strict comparison — no validation code, FR-002/FR-009).

declarations.name: KiSelect
declarations.description:
A form-associated select-only combobox for choosing one option from
declarative `ki-option` children.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).
declarations.whenToUse:
choose exactly one value from a known closed list, especially
when there are roughly five or more choices or space is limited.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
`ki-radio-group` for a few always-visible choices,
`ki-input` for free or searchable text, `ki-checkbox`/`ki-switch` for
binary decisions, or multiselect and command menus.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Prevents opening, removes the trigger from keyboard reach, and excludes
the select from form submission. Boolean presence semantics apply.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description:
Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` select is left
without a choice, and its `validationMessage` ("Choose a country").
Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An
error set with `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; call
`setCustomValidity` for those.

attributes.name: help-text
attributes.description:
One line of help under the trigger, read with it as the combobox
description: what the choice decides. While an error shows, the error
takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Visible label and accessible-name source for the combobox trigger.
When NOT to use: do not omit it; unlabeled selects are invalid usage.

attributes.name: label-hint
attributes.description:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the
combobox name, so people know before submitting whether to choose:
"(optional)" on the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or
"(required)" the other way round, in the page's own language. It changes
no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions in it (use `help-text`), errors
(use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key used when a selected option contributes its value.
When NOT to use: omit it when the select should not submit data.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description:
Text shown while no option is selected.
When NOT to use: do not use it as a replacement for `label`.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description:
Requires a non-empty submitted value. The platform validation message is
donated by a hidden native select.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed trigger size (`--ki-select-{size}-*` tokens): the trigger is
24, 32, 40, 48 or 56px tall in onmars, with its padding, radius, text and
indicator; the label and help text follow in three steps. The listbox
and its options keep their size. An unrecognized value matches no style
rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Live projection of the selected option value, or `""` when unselected.
Assigning it selects the first matching option silently; the attribute is
the reset/default declaration and is not updated by user commits.

declarations.name: KiSkeleton
declarations.description: Decorative placeholder shapes that reserve space for loading content.
declarations.whenToUse:
Reserve the expected layout of a card, list, or assistant reply
while it loads. Give the surrounding region an accessible name and set
its aria-busy state. Show the skeleton after about 300 ms of waiting.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
For a standalone loading announcement, progress measurement,
or interactive control. Put content and loading feedback in the caller's region.

attributes.name: animated
attributes.description:
Sweep a highlight while the user permits motion. Set false to use a static
placeholder. Shimmer also stops under reduced motion and forced colours.

attributes.name: block-size
attributes.description:
CSS length for the block axis. For text, this is the height of each line.
Use it to reserve the height of the content that will replace the shape.

attributes.name: inline-size
attributes.description:
CSS length for the inline axis. Use it to match a fixed content width.
Text and rectangles otherwise fill available inline space.

attributes.name: lines
attributes.description:
Number of text lines. Use a whole number from 1 to 20 for the expected
paragraph length. Extra lines are ignored for circles and rectangles.

attributes.name: shape
attributes.description: Match the placeholder to the expected text, avatar, or rectangular content.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
CSS length shared by both axes. Use it for circles or square blocks.
An axis-specific override takes precedence.

declarations.name: KiSpinner
declarations.description: A compact status for an indeterminate wait.
declarations.whenToUse:
show brief inline activity such as saving a change or running a
tool. Choose typing dots for an assistant that is thinking. Set a localized
label that names the activity and mount the spinner when the wait starts.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
use ki-progress for page-level work or a known fraction of
a task. Use ki-alert for persistent notices.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Localized name of the ongoing activity, such as "Saving changes".
Supply a meaningful label for every spinner, even when the text is hidden.
Use the activity's name whenever it can be more specific than "Loading".

attributes.name: show-label
attributes.description:
Display the label beside the graphic when sighted users also need the
activity description. The same text names the status in either case.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Diameter of the ring. Choose the size that fits the surrounding content.
Dots use a fixed size. Unrecognized values draw the medium ring.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
Use a ring for general inline activity and dots for assistant typing or
thinking. Unrecognized values draw a ring.

declarations.name: KiStatus
declarations.description: A tiny, non-interactive status dot that marks the state of a nearby item.
declarations.whenToUse:
mark a state with minimal footprint adjacent to (or overlaid
on) the item it describes: presence on an avatar, health of a service
list entry, connection state in a toolbar. Label it (`label`) or pair it
with adjacent visible text — color is never the only carrier of the
meaning (WCAG 1.4.1).
declarations.whenNotToUse:
short labeled status text (that pill is ki-badge — this dot
never renders text), notification counters or the overlay attachment
mechanism (a future, separate nav-badge concern), messages that need
attention or announcement (ki-alert — the dot has no live region),
progress or loading (ki-progress). An unlabeled dot without adjacent
visible text is an authoring mistake (WCAG 1.4.1).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name for the state ("Online", "Build failing"). With a
label the dot is exposed to assistive technology as a named
non-interactive image (role `img`); without one it is decorative and
contributes nothing to the accessibility tree — the meaning must then
live in adjacent visible text (FR-003, FR-008). The label is never
rendered visually: visible status text belongs to ki-badge. Runtime
changes are not announced (no live region, FR-005).

attributes.name: ring
attributes.description:
Draws a separating ring around the dot for placement over media (an
avatar photo), keeping it distinguishable from the pixels beneath. A
per-instance functional axis — MarsUI ships Outline=True|False as
sibling variants under one theme (recorded deviation from the 002
token-only rule) — while ring width and color stay per-theme
`--ki-status-ring-*` tokens. The ring paints outside the dot's box and
never shifts layout.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description:
Semantic intent, never appearance: each tone resolves its fill from
the per-theme `--ki-status-{tone}-color` tokens. An unrecognized value
matches no style selector, so the dot keeps the neutral appearance
(fallback by CSS construction — no validation code, FR-007).

cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the danger tone fill: Surface/danger_med_em, the exact variable bound to the Type=danger Status variant (Danger/500).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-info-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the info tone fill: Surface/info_high_em (Info/600 light, Info/400 dark) — one step above the med-em 500 pattern the success and danger tones follow, because Info/500 reads 2.29:1 on the light page and WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of the dot (FR-008). No Figma Status variant ships an info Type, so the fill remains an extrapolation onto the Info ramp (001 contract, 010/015 precedent) declared for founder ratification.

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-neutral-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the neutral tone fill: ki.outline.control, the semantic 3:1 non-text floor (Black/48 light, White/48 dark; md.sys.color.outline in material3) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Surface/disabled_high_em (Gray/500 light, White/32 dark), which reads 2.10:1 and 2.78:1 against the page where WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of the dot (FR-008). MarsUI's disabled gray still maps to the charter neutral tone (spec Assumptions).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-radius
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the status component for the dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the round dot is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-ring-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the separating ring: Outline/inverse_black, the exact variable bound to Outline=True variants — white over light surfaces, black over dark ones, so the ring reads as a cutout from the underlying media (FR-002).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-ring-width
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the status component for the separating ring: the 2px stroke on every Outline=True Status variant (FR-002).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-shadow
cssProperties.description: shadow used by the status component for the dot effects: the exact MarsUI pair on every Status variant — e1 drop (0/1/1/-0.5 in the scheme shadow color) plus inner White/12 highlight (0/3/3), i.e. Component_effect/primary_default's box-shadow layers. The effect's backdrop blur is deliberately NOT applied: a 4px dot has no glass surface to blur (brief §5 perf note, glass restraint).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the status component for the dot: the MarsUI 4px dot, Space/xs bound to every Status variant (specs/021-ki-status/design-extraction.md). One size per theme, never an attribute (FR-006).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-success-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the success tone fill: Surface/success_med_em, the exact variable bound to the Type=success Status variant (Success/500).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-warning-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the warning tone fill: Text/warning_high_em (Warning/800 light, Warning/300 dark) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Surface/warning_med_em (Warning/500), which reads 1.92:1 on the light page. No warning surface step clears the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of the dot (Warning/600 reads 2.33:1), so the fill takes the warning ink that is legible on the page (FR-008).

declarations.name: KiSwitch
declarations.description:
A token-styled switch for immediate on/off settings.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).
declarations.whenToUse:
binary settings whose change takes effect immediately, always
with a slotted label.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
selections collected for later form submission; use
ki-checkbox for recorded choices, ki-radio-group for mutually exclusive
choices, and ki-button for actions.

attributes.name: checked
attributes.description:
Live on/off state. Boolean presence semantics apply: any present
`checked` attribute value, including `checked="false"` or malformed
agent output, means on. Omit the attribute to express off.
When to use: set the initial on state for a setting that applies
immediately.
When NOT to use: do not use a switch for choices saved only on submit;
use ki-checkbox for that pattern.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Prevents toggling, removes the switch from keyboard reach, excludes it
from form data, and exposes the unavailable state to assistive technology.
When to use: make a setting temporarily unavailable while preserving its
current state.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending or loading states.

attributes.name: help-text
attributes.description:
One line of help under the switch, read with it as its description: what
turning it on changes.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label. A switch has no constraint of
its own, so it takes no error text; an error the application sets with
`setCustomValidity` shows in this line's place.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key contributed while the switch is on.
When to use: include the immediate setting in native form data when on.
When NOT to use: omit when no form entry should be submitted.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed size: the track is 32 x 18, 40 x 22, 48 x 26 or 56 x 32px in
onmars (`xl` is the design's mobile size), with its thumb. `sm` also takes
the smaller label (13/20, 8px away). An unrecognized value matches no
style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the text and controls around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Form-data value submitted while on. Omit for native checkbox parity: the
submitted value defaults to `on`.
When to use: submit a domain-specific value instead of the default `on`.
When NOT to use: do not set a value to represent off; off contributes
nothing.

attributes.name: disabled

Boolean presence semantics apply: `disabled="false"` is still disabled.

to choose an initial tab; author-set `selected` is overwritten.

declarations.name: KiTabs
declarations.description: A tab group for switching between peer content views.
declarations.whenToUse:
switch between small sets of peer views inside the same page,
with one visible panel at a time.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
selecting form values
(use `ki-radio-group`), page navigation (use links), step flows, or
standalone `ki-tab` / `ki-tab-panel` children outside this group.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Accessible name for the tablist. Always provide one when multiple tab
groups may appear in a view. When NOT to use: do not use `label` as a
visible heading; render visible context in surrounding content.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed strip size: every `ki-tab` it holds is 24, 32, 40, 48 or
56px tall in onmars, with its text, and the gap between tabs follows.
The strip decides for all its tabs; a tab has no size of its own. An
unrecognized value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the controls around the strip.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

declarations.name: KiTextarea
declarations.description:
A token-styled multiline text field with native form semantics.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).
declarations.whenToUse:
free-form text longer than one line, such as comments,
descriptions, messages, delivery notes, or addresses when paired with a
matching `autocomplete` purpose.
declarations.whenNotToUse:
single-line values (`ki-input`), constrained choices,
rich or formatted text editing, or search boxes.

Agent note: initial text is declared through the `value` attribute; element
text content is ignored. Enter inserts a line break and never submits the
enclosing form, the inverse of `ki-input`.

attributes.name: autocomplete
attributes.description:
Autofill detail token forwarded to the native textarea.
When to use: expose entry purpose such as `street-address` when available.
When NOT to use: omit when no valid autofill purpose applies.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description:
Disables editing, focus, validation and form-data contribution.
When to use: make a field temporarily unavailable. When NOT to use: do not
use disabled for readonly review text that should submit.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description:
Message shown in place of the help text once the person's answer fails a
constraint (`required`), and the field's `validationMessage`. Say how to
fix the answer. Without it the browser's own message shows, in the
browser's language. An error set with `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; call
`setCustomValidity` for those.

attributes.name: help-text
attributes.description:
One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: what
to write, or how long. While an error shows, the error takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Visible label rendered by the component and used as the accessible name.
When to use: always provide a concise label for the requested long-form
text. When NOT to use: do not substitute placeholder text for the label.

attributes.name: label-hint
attributes.description:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the field's
name, so people know before submitting whether to answer: "(optional)" on
the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or "(required)" the
other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation;
set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions or length limits in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description:
Form-data key used when the textarea submits with a form.
When to use: provide for fields whose text must be included in FormData.
When NOT to use: omit for display-only or client-only fields.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description:
Hint shown while the textarea is empty.
When to use: add an example or short formatting hint. When NOT to use: do
not use placeholder as the accessible name or required instruction.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description:
Makes the textarea focusable and selectable while rejecting edits.
When to use: show submitted or policy text that should still be included
in form data. When NOT to use: do not use readonly to remove a field from
submission; use disabled.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description:
Requires a non-empty value before form submission.
When to use: mark mandatory long-form text. When NOT to use: do not pair
with `readonly` expecting it to block; readonly fields are validation
exempt like native textareas.

attributes.name: rows
attributes.description:
Visible line count. Invalid, non-numeric, zero, or negative values fall
back to 2; no auto-grow or user resize handle exists in v1.
When to use: set the stable multiline height needed by the layout. When
NOT to use: do not use rows as a responsive size axis.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Token-backed field size (`--ki-textarea-{size}-*` tokens): padding,
radius and text; the label and help text follow in three steps. The
height stays `rows` lines. An unrecognized value matches no style rule
and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Live current text. The `value` attribute declares the reset default;
element text content is ignored. Programmatic assignments replace the
display and emit no events.
When to use: preload or read free-form text, line breaks included. When
NOT to use: do not put initial text between the element tags.

cssProperties.name: --ki-density-control-offset
cssProperties.description: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.

cssProperties.name: --ki-density-target-min
cssProperties.description: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
